package_info.package_versions: unknown (multiple versions affected, as per public advisories)
package_info.why_malicious: The SolarWinds Orion platform was compromised to include the Sunburst backdoor, which enabled attackers to gain unauthorized access to networks, exfiltrate data, and move laterally within affected organizations. The malicious code was inserted into legitimate software updates, making the entire package a vehicle for a sophisticated supply chain attack. The backdoor was stealthily embedded in the SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll, allowing attackers to remotely control infected systems and evade detection for months.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (after installation, during normal Orion operation, typically as a service or scheduled task)
execution_context.file_location: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll (maliciously modified DLL within the Orion platform, typically located in the Orion installation directory)
required_permissions: filesystem (read system and application files, write temporary files)
environment_vars (read system and user environment variables)
process (spawn or control subprocesses for command execution)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: The code first checks for a safe execution environment using anti-analysis and anti-sandbox techniques to avoid detection. If deemed safe, it dynamically generates or retrieves a command-and-control (C2) domain, collects detailed system and environment information (including hostnames, running processes, and network configuration), and exfiltrates this data to the C2 server. The code then polls for attacker-supplied commands and, if received, executes them on the compromised system, enabling remote code execution, lateral movement, and further compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code employs stealthy anti-analysis checks to evade detection, establishes outbound network connections to dynamically generated or attacker-controlled domains, exfiltrates sensitive system and environment information, and enables remote command execution. The use of obfuscated communication, delayed execution, and conditional logic to avoid sandboxes are all hallmarks of advanced persistent threat (APT) malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Orion DLLs should not contain code that initiates outbound connections to non-SolarWinds domains, collects and exfiltrates system information, or executes arbitrary remote commands. Such behaviors are not part of normal telemetry, update, or monitoring operations and represent a clear violation of expected software behavior.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate Orion components may contact SolarWinds servers for updates or telemetry, but these communications are to known, documented domains, use transparent protocols, and do not involve obfuscated logic, anti-analysis checks, or remote command execution capabilities.
key_indicators: Obfuscated or stealthy network communication to dynamically generated or non-SolarWinds domains
Conditional execution logic to evade sandboxes or analysis environments
Outbound DNS and HTTP/S requests to attacker-controlled infrastructure (e.g., avsvmcloud.com)
Collection and exfiltration of detailed system and environment information
Ability to receive and execute arbitrary attacker-supplied commands via C2
Delayed or staged execution to avoid detection during initial analysis

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is inserted into the SolarWinds Orion DLL (SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll) and distributed to customers via a legitimate software update mechanism.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of the Sunburst backdoor code on customer systems upon installation or update

attack_chain.action: The backdoor code performs anti-analysis checks to determine if it is running in a safe environment, then establishes contact with a command-and-control (C2) server using obfuscated or delayed network communication.
attack_chain.leads_to: Stealthy exfiltration of system information and establishment of a persistent C2 channel

attack_chain.action: The backdoor exfiltrates collected system and environment data to the C2 server and polls for attacker-supplied commands.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote execution of attacker commands, enabling lateral movement, data theft, and further compromise of the environment

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network connections from Orion processes, especially to domains not owned by SolarWinds
Orion DLLs (e.g., SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll) making DNS queries to suspicious or dynamically generated domains
Orion process executing commands or scripts outside of normal update or monitoring operations
Presence of obfuscated, delayed, or conditional execution logic within Orion DLLs
Collection and transmission of detailed system/environment information by Orion processes
file_indicators: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll with hash values not matching known-good versions (as per SolarWinds advisories and threat intelligence feeds)
Presence of DLLs with known Sunburst IOCs (e.g., file hashes, digital signature anomalies)
Modified Orion update files or installer packages containing unexpected or unauthorized code
network_indicators: DNS queries to avsvmcloud.com and related Sunburst C2 domains (as listed in public IOCs)
HTTP/S traffic from Orion processes to attacker-controlled infrastructure, including but not limited to avsvmcloud.com
Unusual Orion process network activity, such as connections to external IPs/domains not associated with SolarWinds
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor Orion-related processes for unexpected outbound network connections, especially DNS or HTTP/S requests to known Sunburst C2 domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com) and other IOCs from threat intelligence feeds. Regularly verify file hashes of SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll and other Orion DLLs against known-good values. Inspect Orion DLLs for obfuscated or delayed execution logic and anti-analysis techniques. Use endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools to alert on Orion processes executing commands or scripts outside of normal operations. Block or alert on known Sunburst IOCs at both the network and file level, and review update packages for unauthorized modifications.
